I think we disagree fundamentally on what a good prompt is.

For me, a prompt is meant to prompt something beautiful - not a story. As you can tell from the post I made, there was no story in that. It was just the expanding of the prompt - to make something beautiful out of a shortly worded statement.

Prompts, I think, come in all sorts. There are narrative prompts, which make you write stories and create narratives - there are descriptive prompts, such as the one I posted, in which you are trying to put to words either a beautiful image or an idea. Then there are puzzle-like prompts, in which you are to think of creative ways around a dilemma that is dictated by the prompt-creator.

I'm just not sure that prompts can only come in the form of narrative prompts - surely, there are more forms of writing than purely narrative ones.
